At this file's 59.26% stopping, 40.74% remain, so new starts are 2,863, 43,208 = 44,374 - 2,863 x 0.4074, and 50,632 = 68,708 - 44,374 x 0.4074. The pool is 1,200,448 less cumulative starts: 1,197,585 in 2025 and 1,154,377 in 2026. Capture: 3.608% in 2025 and 4.386% in 2026, which is the anchor. CROSS-CHECK: the revenue basis counts 3.95 Cobenfy patients per 2025 Part D beneficiary (44,374 against 11,246), which is where the convention may overstate the patient count. MULTIPLE 0.4, A JUDGEMENT: 0.4 x 4.386% = 1.754% of the untreated pool, the multiple the book puts on emraclidine, the other muscarinic entrant that would launch about nine years after Cobenfy. For more: Novartis lists GXV813 as an M4 agonist, where Cobenfy pairs xanomeline, 'a M1/M4 muscarinic agonist', with trospium, 'a peripheral muscarinic antagonist' (BMY 10-K), and Novartis has the scale to sell it. Against: STAR-1 is the first test of efficacy and has not read out; M4 selectivity has not yet been proven in a trial, since emraclidine's two Phase 2 EMPOWER trials missed their primary endpoint (AbbVie 10-K 0001551152-26-000008); and Cobenfy's combination patents expire in 2030, or 2033 if a pending term restoration is granted (BMY 10-K), so the class may carry a generic by the time GXV813 sells
